title: savor it
subtitle: stay with a good moment a little longer

steps.prompt: where can gratitude point, besides outward?
steps.answer: inward: a quiet thanks for small things done today.

steps.text: here's a small skill for the good moments.
minds tend to skip past what went well. savoring is staying with a good moment a little longer, on purpose.
think of one small good moment from today or yesterday. got one?

options.label: yes
options.reply: lovely. hold it in mind for a moment.

options.label: a small one
options.reply: small is perfect. a warm drink counts.

options.label: not really
options.reply: that's okay. try one from this week, or something to look forward to.

steps.text: psychologists fred bryant and joseph veroff describe savoring as a skill. it can point three ways: looking forward to something, staying in a moment, and remembering one.
steps.evidence: a well-studied idea; practices are still being tested

steps.prompt: pick any ways to stay with it:
options: remember what you could see and hear
tell yourself what you liked about it
let yourself smile, if it comes
steps.reply: take a few seconds with it now. no rush.

steps.text: in one study, students who practiced savoring good moments for two weeks reported less low mood than those who didn't.
when something small goes well today, pause and stay with it for three breaths.

grounding.idea: a two-week savoring practice reduced depressive symptoms and negative feelings
grounding.source: Hurley & Kwon, 2012, Journal of Happiness Studies
